chart.cap_above_tipping: Above the tipping point the recommendation no longer changes – however high the costs go.
chart.cap_all_optimal: Here every deductible is the cheapest at some level of healthcare costs.
chart.cap_never_optimal: Only the deductibles **{winners} CHF** are the cheapest, depending on the costs. The faded ones ({never} CHF) are at no level of healthcare costs.
chart.cap_no_tipping: The lowest deductible ({deductible} CHF) never pays off in the range shown.
chart.cap_red_line: The red line marks your expected healthcare costs ({amount} CHF); you can adjust the amount above. The cheapest deductible there is drawn in bold.
chart.cap_tipping: The grey dashed line is the tipping point: from **{tipping} CHF** the {low} CHF deductible pays off, below it the {other} CHF one. Between the best and the worst deductible lie up to {spread} CHF per year.
chart.cap_tipping_several: The grey dashed line is the tipping point: from **{tipping} CHF** the {low} CHF deductible pays off, below it a higher one, depending on the costs (see chart). Between the best and the worst deductible lie up to {spread} CHF per year.

disclaimer.body:
From
the official premium data the app works out what the person described would pay at the
healthcare costs given – no more than that. Which insurance suits someone depends
on things that do not appear here:

- **Premium reductions**, supplementary insurance, the hospital contribution of
  CHF 15 per day, and the particulars of individual models.
- **Restrictions on the choice of doctor.** The alternative models are included in
  the premiums, but their conditions are not evaluated. The cheapest offer is not
  automatically the most suitable – the cheapest are almost always models that
  restrict the choice of doctor.
- **Children on different deductibles.** If children with the same insurer
  have different deductibles, the insurer sets the joint limit on their cost sharing
  itself (Art. 93 para. 3 KVV). That limit is not published, so the app calculates
  without it. With the same deductible for all the children, the statutory limit is
  included.
- **Higher coinsurance for some medicines.** If a medicine costs at least 10% more than the average of the cheapest third of products with the same active ingredient, coinsurance is 40% instead of 10%. The app uses 10% throughout.
- **Pregnancy.** From the 13th week of pregnancy until eight weeks after the birth, neither deductible nor coinsurance is charged (Art. 64 para. 7 KVG). The app still counts both.
- **The tipping point is exact to the franc, but the difference there is in
  centimes.** The direction it indicates – high or low deductible – is reliable, the
  precise amount is not.

What counts is what the insurers state and the official
[priminfo.admin.ch]({priminfo}). For a decision with consequences, advice from an
independent body is worth it.

form.accident_help: If you are insured against accidents elsewhere – for instance because you work at least 8 hours a week for the same employer – choose “without”. Otherwise “with”.
form.birth_year_help: The year of birth counts, not the age: whoever turns 18 or younger in {year} pays children's premiums; whoever turns 19 to 25, premiums for young adults.

form.expected_costs_help: The full invoice amounts for doctor, hospital, medication and therapy under basic insurance – not just what you paid yourself. They decide which deductible pays off.

form.tariff_models_help: The standard model gives you free choice of doctor. The other models restrict it (family doctor, practice or phone first) and are usually cheaper for it. Remove what does not suit you.
form.tariff_models_help_pharm: Pharmacy models such as PharMed or KPTwin.win are not a category of their own: the FOPH lists them under practice and family-doctor models or under flexible models.

household.caption: Here you find the annual total costs for everyone in the household: the premiums ({premiums} CHF) plus deductible and coinsurance at the healthcare costs given – each at the recommended offer: the cheapest, or where today's contract is given, the smallest change worth making.
household.family_cap_applied: This includes the limit on cost sharing for children of one family with the same insurer: together at most {cap} CHF ({law}). Here that comes to {saving} CHF.
household.heading: Total household costs
household.sibling_included: The sibling discount is included in the total: with {insurer} – {tariff} on tariff tiers {tiers}, the {count} children cost {total} CHF together instead of {separate} CHF at the standard rate, {saving} CHF less.
household.sibling_included_switch: The sibling discount is included in the total: all {count} children with {insurer} – {tariff} on tariff tiers {tiers} cost {total} CHF together instead of {separate} CHF with each child at its own cheapest provider at the standard rate, {saving} CHF less. The discount only applies when all children are with the same insurer.
household.sibling_not_worth: One insurer for all the children does not pay here: each child on its own cheapest offer costs {separate} CHF in total; all the children with the same insurer cost at least {total} CHF (cheapest with {insurer}).
household.switch_note:
Under “Switch” you see what moving from today's contract to the recommendation in this table brings:

* “Saving/year”: with the current deductible given, the difference in annual total costs (premiums, deductible and coinsurance) at the expected healthcare costs. Without it, only the difference in premium, at the recommended deductible.
* “What changes”: the smallest change that leaves you less than {threshold} CHF above the cheapest offer – first only the deductible, then the model at the same insurer, only then another insurer.

If a switch saves less than {threshold} CHF a year in all, it says “no”: then it is not worth the effort.
household.switch_note_children: For the children the recommendation is the joint one: all with the same insurer, with the sibling discount (see above). The saving refers to that.
household.unknown_tiers: The premium data carries the child tier(s) {tiers}, whose conditions are not known here. They are left out of the calculation – so the sibling discount could be larger than shown below.
lead:
You say which healthcare costs you expect in {year}: doctor, hospital, medication, therapy.

From this, the app works out, for every person in the household, the insurer, model and deductible with the lowest total costs, among the tariff models that suit you. Sibling discounts are included. The calculation uses the FOPH's official premium data ([opendata.swiss]({opendata})). The environmental levy refund ({rebate} CHF per year) is already deducted from all premiums.
loading.premiums: Loading the FOPH premium data. The first time takes a moment, after that it is quick.
metric.caption: Premiums plus deductible and coinsurance at your expected healthcare costs, at the cheapest offer among your tariff models. The offers are further down.
motivation: Why this app exists. I knew that higher expected healthcare costs make a lower deductible sensible, and the other way round. But I did not know at which costs which deductible pays off, so that the growth in my family's health costs could be kept down. That is what I built this app for.

popover.tipping_point_body: That only the lowest and the highest deductible are ever the cheapest is something I have observed for years. A [published formula]({formula}) for the 300 and 2500 steps confirms the tipping point, but compares only those two steps. That the middle deductibles *never* pay off only shows up when every step is calculated – which is what this app does. In the data of recent years it has held every time; because premiums are set anew each year, it can change.
season.closed: 📅 **The {next} premiums come out at the end of September.** Until then the app calculates with the {year} premiums and shows whether today's contract is a good choice. As a rule you can only switch for 1 January {next} – calculate again with the new premiums then; the app picks them up by itself. Only with the lowest deductible ({ordinary_adult} CHF, children {ordinary_child} CHF) in the standard model can you also switch insurer for the end of June, with notice by 31 March.
season.open: 📅 **Switching season for {year}.** For a new insurer, another model or a lower deductible from 1 January {year}, your notice must reach your current insurer by 30 November {deadline_year}. You can switch to a higher deductible until 31 December.
season.stale: The premium data is from {year} and no longer current – the new data could not be loaded yet. The figures may differ from today's premiums.

total_costs_explainer:
**Annual total costs = premiums + deductible + coinsurance.** Up to the amount of the deductible you pay your healthcare costs yourself, of everything above it {rate} (coinsurance), but at most {cap_adult} CHF per year (children: {cap_child} CHF). The insurer pays the rest.

Looking only at the premium gets you nowhere: the higher the deductible, the lower the premium. Which deductible pays off depends on how high your healthcare costs are. Of course you can't know that exactly. Take your costs of recent years as a guide and add what you can see coming: a planned operation, an ongoing therapy, regular medication.
